walkthroughs.body_html:
Measurement & Analysis — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Measurement & Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Measurement & Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What distinguishes structural isomers from stereoisomers?
options: The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
Structural isomers have different atom connectivity; stereoisomers have the same connectivity but different spatial arrangement.
Stereoisomers are just structural isomers drawn from a different angle.
Stereoisomers have different numbers of atoms but the same molecular formula.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell?
options: The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
It completes the circuit by allowing ions to flow between the half-cells, maintaining electrical neutrality.
SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
The salt bridge carries electrons between the two electrodes.

mcqs.q: How does the rate of an SN2 reaction depend on concentrations?
options: Stereoisomers have different numbers of atoms but the same molecular formula.
SN2 reactions are first order overall because only the substrate matters.
SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
Rate is first order in both substrate AND nucleophile (overall second order) because both are involved in the rate-determining step.
